items.title: Exit 8
items.reason: A commuter becomes trapped in an apparently endless subway corridor and must infer and obey a precise anomaly-detection rule set to reach Exit 8. The mystery remains active across most of the runtime because every pass asks the viewer and protagonist to inspect the environment, decide whether reality has changed, and learn the consequences of mistakes. The film broadens the loop through increasingly bizarre anomalies, nonlinear perspectives involving the walking man and the boy, and uncertainty over whether the corridor is real or illusory. Whole-film criticism also identifies an important limitation: the plotting is deliberately threadbare and the narrative does not progressively explain the origin of the phenomenon, so progressive_revelation and cause_uncertainty are kept moderate rather than inflated. Strong containment, unknown rules, clue-puzzling, suspense, reality uncertainty and visual craft still make it a solid baseline-profile match.
